result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks and paved sidewalks, but the overall design prioritizes vehicle throughput with wide lanes and long crossing distances. The lack of pedestrian refuge islands or curb extensions leaves pedestrians exposed to traffic for an extended period.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross a very wide multi-lane roadway without any mid-point refuge, increasing exposure time to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radii
hazards.description: The geometry of the intersection corners allows vehicles to maintain higher speeds while turning, increasing the risk of collisions with pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right and left corners of the intersection

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Islands
interventions.description: Install raised islands in the center of the roadway to provide a safe waiting area and reduce the unprotected crossing distance.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and force drivers to slow down when making turns.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Ensure dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers are installed and visible to provide clear information on crossing time.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure, including a marked zebra crosswalk and a sidewalk in good condition. However, the lack of dedicated pedestrian signals and the relatively wide, open roadway design may compromise safety by allowing for higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Missing pedestrian signals
hazards.description: Pedestrians lack clear guidance on when it is safe to cross the intersection as no walk/don't-walk signals are visible.
hazards.location_in_image: On the signal pole at the intersection

hazards.name: Wide curb radius
hazards.description: The open corner design may encourage vehicles to make turns at higher speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the intersection near the crosswalk

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to reduce the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a sidewalk separated from the roadway by a grass buffer, but is dominated by a wide, multi-lane arterial designed for high-speed traffic. While a bike lane and street lighting are present, the lack of protected crossings or pedestrian signals across the main road poses significant risks to people walking.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground.

hazards.name: High-Speed Road Geometry
hazards.description: Wide travel lanes and a lack of traffic calming measures encourage high vehicle speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway stretching into the distance.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to reduce the unprotected crossing distance and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace standard transverse markings with continental-style high-visibility markings to increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signals with countdown timers at the intersection to provide clear information on crossing time.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-lane signalized intersection with a grass median but a complete lack of visible pedestrian crossing infrastructure. There are no painted crosswalks or pedestrian signals, forcing pedestrians to cross a high-speed environment unprotected.

hazards.name: Unmarked crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic at a signalized intersection without a designated or marked path.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated signal heads for pedestrians are visible, leaving them to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra or ladder style pavement markings to clearly define the pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane or shoulder to reduce crossing distance and improve sight lines.
